21: # Skill Manager v2
22: 
23: Skill Manager uses **git submodules** and the **`mm-skills` GitHub org** to manage AI skills. Each skill is its own repo. Projects declare their skills in `.gitmodules`, and anyone cloning the project gets all skills automatically.
24: 
25: ## Design Philosophy
26: 
27: - **One global skill**: `skill-manager` itself. It lives at `~/.gemini/config/skills/skill-manager/`.
28: - **Everything else is a submodule**: Skills live at `.agents/skills/<name>/` as git submodules.
29: - **Git-native**: No caches, no registries, no custom sync. Just git.
30: - **Cross-harness**: A symlink between `.claude` and `.agents` gives both Gemini and Claude visibility into the same skills.
31: - **Portable**: Anyone cloning a project runs `git submodule update --init` and has every skill.
32: 
33: ## Command Reference
34: 
35: All commands are shell scripts that accept a single JSON argument and return a JSON response. Run them from the project root.
36: 
37: ### `catalog` — Browse Available Skills
38: 
39: Lists all skills in the `mm-skills` GitHub org.
40: 
41: - **When to use:** When the user is looking for a skill, wants to see what's available, or asks "what skills do we have?"
42: - **Input:** `{"query": "optional filter", "org": "mm-skills"}`
43: - **Example:** `run_command('.agents/skills/skill-manager/scripts/catalog.sh \'{}\'')`
44: - **Returns:** `{"org": "mm-skills", "count": N, "skills": [{"name": "...", "description": "...", "url": "...", "visibility": "...", "updated": "..."}]}`
45: 
46: ### `add` — Add a Skill to the Project
47: 
48: Adds a skill as a git submodule. Also ensures a cross-harness symlink between `.agents` and `.claude` (creating whichever is missing).
49: 
50: - **When to use:** To install a new skill. Works with `mm-skills` repos or any git URL.
51: - **Input:** `{"name": "string", "url": "optional custom URL", "project": "optional, defaults to ."}`
52: - **Example:** `run_command('.agents/skills/skill-manager/scripts/add.sh \'{"name": "distillery"}\'')`
53: - **Special:** `{"name": "skill-manager", "global": true}` installs/updates skill-manager globally.
54: - **Returns:** `{"status": "added", "name": "...", "path": ".agents/skills/<name>", "commit": "..."}`
55: 
56: ### `update` — Pull Latest Changes
57: 
58: Updates one or all skills to their latest upstream commit.
59: 
60: - **When to use:** To get the newest version of skills, or when the user says "update my skills."
61: - **Input:** `{"name": "skill-name" or "all", "project": "optional, defaults to ."}`
62: - **Example:** `run_command('.agents/skills/skill-manager/scripts/update.sh \'{"name": "all"}\'')`
63: - **Returns:** `{"updated": [{"name": "...", "from": "sha", "to": "sha", "changed": true|false}]}`

65: ### `status` — Check Sync State

67: Shows the current state of all skills in the project: which are up-to-date, modified, behind, or uninitialized.

70: - **Input:** `{"project": "optional, defaults to ."}`
71: - **Example:** `run_command('.agents/skills/skill-manager/scripts/status.sh \'{}\'')`
72: - **Returns:** `{"project": "...", "skills": [{"name": "...", "commit": "sha", "state": "...", "has_upstream": bool}], "global": {"skill-manager": {...}}}`

74: ### `push` — Push Edits Back Upstream
75: 
76: Commits and pushes local edits to a skill back to its `mm-skills` repo, then updates the parent project's submodule pointer.

80: - **Example:** `run_command('.agents/skills/skill-manager/scripts/push.sh \'{"name": "distillery", "message": "Improve output format"}\'')`

83: ### `fork` — Fork a Skill from a Third-Party Repo
84: 
85: Extracts a skill from a third-party mono-repo (like `anthropics/skills`) using `git subtree split` and creates a new repo in `mm-skills`. Records provenance in `.upstream.json` so you can sync upstream changes later.
86: 
87: - **When to use:** To import a skill from an external source and own it in your org.
88: - **Input:** `{"upstream": "https://github.com/org/repo", "path": "skills/name", "name": "skill-name", "visibility": "private"}`
89: - **Example:** `run_command('.agents/skills/skill-manager/scripts/fork.sh \'{"upstream": "https://github.com/anthropics/skills", "path": "skills/skill-creator", "name": "skill-creator"}\'')`
90: - **Returns:** `{"created": "https://github.com/mm-skills/<name>", "upstream": "...", "commit": "sha"}`
91: 
92: ### `sync` — Check/Merge Upstream Changes
93: 
94: For forked skills (those with `.upstream.json`): checks what's changed upstream and optionally merges those changes into your fork.
95: 
96: - **When to use:** To check if a third-party skill has been updated upstream, or to pull in upstream improvements while preserving your local modifications.
97: - **Input:** `{"name": "string", "action": "check" or "merge", "project": "optional, defaults to ."}`
98: - **Example (check):** `run_command('.agents/skills/skill-manager/scripts/sync.sh \'{"name": "skill-creator", "action": "check"}\'')`

107: - **Input:** `{"name": "string", "project": "optional, defaults to ."}`
108: - **Example:** `run_command('.agents/skills/skill-manager/scripts/remove.sh \'{"name": "terrashark"}\'')`
109: - **Returns:** `{"removed": "...", "status": "removed"}`

111: ### `migrate` — Scan & Convert a Repo to Submodules
112: 
113: Scans an existing repo's `.agents/skills/` directory, cross-references each skill against the `mm-skills` catalog, and optionally converts matching skills from plain directories to submodules. See [references/migration-protocol.md](references/migration-protocol.md) for the full workflow.
114: 
115: - **When to use:** When migrating an existing project that has skills as plain directories (not submodules) to the skill-manager system.
116: - **Input:** `{"project": "/path/to/repo", "action": "scan|execute"}`
117: - **Example (scan):** `run_command('.agents/skills/skill-manager/scripts/migrate.sh \'{"project": "/path/to/repo"}\'')`
118: - **Example (execute):** `run_command('.agents/skills/skill-manager/scripts/migrate.sh \'{"project": "/path/to/repo", "action": "execute"}\'')`
119: - **Returns (scan):** `{"summary": {"match": N, "modified": N, "new": N, "already_submodule": N}, "skills": [...]}`
120: - **Returns (execute):** `{"converted": N, "executed": [...], "skipped": {"modified": [...], "new": [...]}}`
121: - **Categories:**
122:   - `MATCH` — Identical to catalog, safe to auto-convert
123:   - `MODIFIED` — Exists in catalog but local differs (review diffs first)
124:   - `NEW` — Not in catalog (decide: add to catalog or skip)
125:   - `ALREADY` — Already a submodule
126: 
127: ## Common Workflows
128: 
129: ### Setting Up a New Project with Skills
130: 
131: ```bash
132: # 1. Browse what's available
133: catalog '{}'
134: 
135: # 2. Add the skills you need
136: add '{"name": "distillery"}'
137: add '{"name": "principal-architect"}'
138: add '{"name": "embedded-systems"}'
139: 
140: # 3. Commit the .gitmodules and submodules
141: git commit -m "Add project skills"
142: ```
143: 
144: Anyone cloning this project later runs `git submodule update --init` and gets everything.
145: 
146: ### Improving a Skill and Sharing the Changes
147: 
148: ```bash
149: # 1. Edit the SKILL.md or scripts in .agents/skills/<name>/
150: # 2. Push the changes back to the skill's repo
151: push '{"name": "distillery", "message": "Improve distillation prompts"}'
152: # This commits in the submodule, pushes to mm-skills/distillery,
153: # and updates the parent project's submodule pointer.
154: ```
155: 
156: ### Importing a Third-Party Skill
157: 
158: ```bash
159: # 1. Fork it from the upstream mono-repo into mm-skills
160: fork '{"upstream": "https://github.com/anthropics/skills", "path": "skills/skill-creator", "name": "skill-creator"}'
161: 
162: # 2. Add it to your project
163: add '{"name": "skill-creator"}'
164: 
165: # 3. Later, check for upstream updates
166: sync '{"name": "skill-creator", "action": "check"}'
167: 
168: # 4. Merge upstream changes (preserves your local modifications)
169: sync '{"name": "skill-creator", "action": "merge"}'
170: ```
171: 
172: ### Updating All Skills
173: 
174: ```bash
175: # Update everything to latest
176: update '{"name": "all"}'
177: 
178: # Update skill-manager itself (global)
179: update '{"name": "skill-manager"}'
180: ```
181: 
182: ### Migrating an Existing Repo
183: 
184: ```bash
185: # 1. Scan to see what's there
186: migrate '{"project": "/path/to/repo"}'
187: 
188: # 2. Handle MODIFIED skills (push local changes upstream first)
189: # 3. Handle NEW skills (create repos or fork from upstream)
190: 
191: # 4. Execute the migration (converts MATCH skills to submodules)
192: migrate '{"project": "/path/to/repo", "action": "execute"}'
193: 
194: # 5. Commit the result
195: git add .gitmodules .agents/skills/
196: git commit -m "Migrate skills to submodules"
197: ```
198: 
199: ## Cross-Harness Support
200: 
201: Skills live at `.agents/skills/<name>/`. Both Gemini and Claude can discover them:
202: 
203: - **Gemini/AGY**: Reads from `.agents/skills/` directly
204: - **Claude Code**: Reads from `.claude/skills/` via a symlink
205: 
206: The `add` command creates this symlink automatically, handling three scenarios:
207: 
208: | Scenario | What happens |
209: |---|---|
210: | Only `.agents/` exists | Creates `.claude → .agents` symlink |
211: | Only `.claude/` exists | Creates `.agents → .claude` symlink |
212: | Both exist independently | Errors — you must remove or merge one first |
213: 
214: 
215: ## Error Handling
216: 
217: All scripts return JSON errors to stderr with `"error"` and `"hint"` fields. Common issues:
218: 
219: - **"Not a git repository"**: Run from within a git project, or pass `"project": "/path/to/project"`.
220: - **"gh not found"**: Install the GitHub CLI (`brew install gh`) and authenticate (`gh auth login`).
221: - **"Submodule already exists"**: The skill is already added. Use `update` instead.
222: - **"No .upstream.json"**: `sync` only works on forked skills. Use `update` for `mm-skills` repos.
223: 
224: ## Contributing to Skills
225: 
226: When a user wants to report a bug, suggest a change, submit a PR, or asks about licensing — read [references/contributing-protocol.md](references/contributing-protocol.md) for the full contribution protocol and guidance.
227: 
228: ## Dependencies
229: 
230: - `git` — for submodule operations
231: - `jq` — for JSON parsing
232: - `gh` — GitHub CLI, for `catalog` and `fork` commands (install via `brew install gh`)

  "body": "## Problem

Once the architect approves a PR (`bug-fixer:architect:approved`, undrafted via `gh pr ready`), it exits the architect loop entirely and sits in the human maintainer's queue. If `main` advances (e.g., another PR merges), the approved PR can develop **merge conflicts** that block the review and merge — and nobody detects it.

## Proposed Solution: Conflict Monitor in Architect Tick Cycle

Add a **new Step 0.5** to `architect_dispatcher.py` that runs on every tick (every 15 min), **before** the existing draft-PR review logic. This step queries all approved-but-unmerged PRs and checks their GitHub `mergeable` status.

---

## Design Decisions

### Detection Method: GitHub `mergeable` field

GitHub's API provides a `mergeable` field on PRs, computed asynchronously. Possible values:
- `"MERGEABLE"` — no conflicts
- `"CONFLICTING"` — merge conflicts exist
- `"UNKNOWN"` — GitHub hasn't computed it yet (retry next tick)

This is the lightest option — no local git operations, no worktrees needed. The 15-minute tick cadence is perfect for retrying `UNKNOWN` states.

### Response: Route back through the existing state machine

When a conflict is detected:

1. **Post an `[ARCHITECT]` comment** explaining the conflict
2. **Remove `bug-fixer:architect:approved`** — PR is no longer ready to merge
3. **Add `bug-fixer:engineer:needs-iteration`** — signals the engineering dispatcher to pick it up
4. **Convert PR back to draft** (`gh pr ready --undo`) — re-enters the architect's draft-PR query on the next cycle after engineering fixes

This cleanly re-enters the existing state machine:
```
Approved (conflicting) → needs-iteration → engineering rework → draft PR → architect re-review → approved
```

### Why NOT auto-rebase?

- A rebase can introduce subtle semantic conflicts that pass `git merge` but break tests
- The engineering agent should rebase, run tests, and verify — same as any other iteration
- Keeps the system simple — one path for all rework

---

## Files to Modify

### 1. `scripts/architect_dispatcher.py`

Add **Step 0.5: Merge Conflict Monitor** between the sweep (Step 0, line 127) and the draft-PR polling (line 132). The new code:

- Queries open PRs with labels `bug-fixer:engineer:pr` + `bug-fixer:architect:approved`
- For each, checks GitHub's `mergeable` status via the JSON API
- If `CONFLICTING`: posts `[ARCHITECT]` comment, removes approved label, adds needs-iteration label, converts back to draft
- If `UNKNOWN`: logs and retries next tick
- If `MERGEABLE`: logs clean status

### 2. `docs/label-taxonomy.md`

Update the state machine diagram to show the new conflict-detection transition:
```
architect_approved --> engineer_needs_iteration : Merge conflict detected
```

Update the Dispatcher Routing Table to document that the architect dispatcher now also monitors approved PRs for conflicts.

### 3. `skills/architect-review/SKILL.md` — No changes needed

Conflict detection happens entirely in the dispatcher (no LLM involvement).

### 4. `rules/AGENTS.md` — No changes needed

`gh pr ready --undo` is not a merge command, and rebase behavior is covered by Rule 12 (Main-Only Branching).

---

## Edge Cases

| Scenario | Handling |
|---|---|
| `mergeable` is `UNKNOWN` | Log and retry on next 15-min tick |
| PR has `needs-intervention` + `approved` | Conflict check removes `approved` and adds `needs-iteration`. Human-escalated PRs aren't auto-claimed — correct. |
| Multiple approved PRs conflict | Each handled independently in its own worktree |
| Conflict on round 5 | `[ARCHITECT]` comment increments review counter. After 5 rounds → `human:needs-intervention`. Intentional. |

## Implementation Notes

- **No new labels needed** — reuses `engineer:needs-iteration` and removes `architect:approved`
- **No LLM cost** — conflict detection is pure `gh` CLI calls in the dispatcher
- **No new dependencies** — uses only existing GitHub API JSON fields
- **Idempotent** — running twice on the same conflicting PR is harmless
- **`gh pr ready --undo`** — standard CLI method to convert a ready PR back to draft
